title: Sustain humane care when improvement is not the assignment

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Endurance can mean preserving humane care under an unresolved constraint. It does not require passivity toward an available remedy or denying a need to stop an unsafe situation.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional ordinary repair delay: a household reading lamp is being repaired; safe existing room lighting remains available. Provider promised an update Friday and accepts one status inquiry. Jo’s care floor is normal meals, existing care arrangements and one protected rest opening; no treatment change is involved. Monday rest occurs, Wednesday a necessary errand displaces it, Friday a wanted friend call occurs. Repair completion is unknown.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Review the three points, identify missed care and choose between waiting, a proportionate inquiry and practical support. Do not set an improvement quota.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person calls ignoring an urgent accessible help route “patience.” Does endurance require continued waiting?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Waiting for the promised update can be reasonable; an inquiry is also within the offered route. Wednesday’s missed rest remains a support/capacity question. Friday company does not repair the lamp. Partial: call all planned care completed. Incorrect: insist endurance forbids asking or that a small comfort solves every strain. If essential safety were affected, this nonurgent waiting case would no longer fit.
criteria: Care and unresolved outcome are tracked separately
Missed care informs support rather than character judgment

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Respond to the actual urgency through suitable help. The value of patient care does not override an immediate need or turn avoidable neglect into virtue.
